observation_summary: The OpenMapRealMatrix constructor fails to throw a NumberIsTooLargeException when initialized with dimensions that cause an integer overflow in the internal key computation, as demonstrated by the failing test case.
hypothesis: The constructor for OpenMapRealMatrix lacks a validation check (guard) to ensure that the product of the matrix dimensions does not exceed the maximum value representable by an integer, leading to an integer overflow during key calculation.
prediction: The fix will involve adding an 'if' statement or a similar validation check in the constructor to verify that the dimensions are within valid bounds before proceeding with the internal key calculation.
experiment_rationale: The test case explicitly expects a NumberIsTooLargeException when passing Integer.MAX_VALUE as a dimension. The failure to throw this exception confirms that the code is missing a boundary check for the input parameters.
reasoning_summary: The bug is a classic missing boundary check. The code fails to validate input parameters (matrix dimensions) against the constraints of the internal data structure (integer-based key mapping), resulting in an overflow. This is a quintessential 'Checking' defect as it involves missing validation logic for input data.
evidence_used: Bug report description: Integer overflow in OpenMapRealMatrix

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the key computation is the site of the overflow, the root cause is the lack of validation on the input parameters that feed into that computation.
This is a local validation issue, not a design-level capability gap or a missing class/object.
